articles.title: Carrot Top lawyer says comedian was extorted days before suicide attempt
articles.summary: Carrot Top's lawyer filed an emergency motion to prevent his alleged extortionist from filing court documents after the comedian's suicide attempt.
articles.body:
Carrot Top 's lawyer has filed an emergency motion to prevent his alleged extortionist and former friend, Brian Evans, from filing more documents.

Attorney Ronnie Bitman asked a Florida court to enforce "immediate gatekeeping procedures" in Evans' ongoing case against the 61-year-old comedian, born Scott Thompson, according to documents obtained by USA TODAY. Bitman cited Thompson's Sept. 18 suicide attempt , which left him hospitalized.

"This is now an emergency in the most human sense," the motion read. "A public filing can become national news almost immediately. This has been Evans' modus operandi in repeatedly extorting Mr. Thompson with the threat ofexposing him to ill repute, false allegations, and salacious materials."

See comedian Carrot Top in photos amid hospitalization

If you or someone you know may be experiencing a mental health crisis, contact the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline by dialing or texting “988.” Carrot Top , 61, is currently recovering in the hospital after an alleged suicide attempt. The comedian, whose real name is Scott Christopher Thompson, allegedly attempted suicide in Las Vegas on Friday, Sept. 19, and was taken to a local hospital, where he's receiving care, according to TMZ , which reported the news first. Scroll to look back on Carrot Top's career in red carpet moments.

Lawyer says Carrot Top's mental state was impacted by Brian Evans' lawsuit

Bitman said Thompson's mental health decline was a result of repeated threats by Evans that he will publicize an alleged sexually explicit video of the actor and other "private, personal secrets" in exchange for money.

According to emails submitted with the filing, Evans – who sued Thompson two years ago to reverse a previous settlement deal and is representing himself in the matter – has demanded millions of dollars between 2024 and the days leading up to Thompson's suicide attempt.

Calling Evans a "serial filer who abuses the Court system," Bitman said "ordinary remedies" for "after-the-fact relief is not enough." Bitman requested the court restrict Evans' ability to file any new documents without the court's approval, including barring him from the ability to e-file.

"The threatened injury here - continued publication of intensely private material on a docket monitored by national media - cannot be repaired after publication," Bitman added.

USA TODAY reached out to Evans for comment.

Carrot Top is hospitalized for attempting suicide

Thompson's publicist Jami Schlicher told USA TODAY in a Sept. 21 statement that he "remains hospitalized and under close medical care" but is "breathing on his own and continuing to improve, surrounded by his family and those closest to him."

The stand-up star – known for his curly red hair, satirical comedy and use of props – rose to fame in the '90s and has continued to build a successful career. When news of his suicide attempt was reported last week, Thompson was on his long-running comedy residency at Luxor Hotel and Casino.

"Humor has always been such an important part of who Scott is and how he connects with people, and that remains true today as he shares moments of humor with the medical staff caring for him," Schlicher said. "Many messages from fans have been shared with Scott, including stories from people about how his comedy helped them through difficult periods in their own lives. Hearing those stories and feeling that support has meant a great deal to him during his recovery."The statement concluded, "Scott and his family remain deeply grateful for the extraordinary kindness and continue to ask that his privacy be respected."

If you or someone you know may be struggling with suicidal thoughts, you can call 988 any time day or night, or chat online. Crisis Text Line also provides free, 24/7, confidential support via text message to people in crisis when they dial 741741.

articles.summary: Lionel Richie underwent a heart procedure leading to the postponement of at least three shows and casting doubt on an upcoming Las Vegas residency, a representative for the famed singer and producer said Tuesday.
articles.body: Lionel Richie underwent a heart procedure leading to the postponement of at least three shows and casting doubt on an upcoming Las Vegas residency, a representative for the famed singer and producer said Tuesday. Richie was scheduled to perform with Earth, Wind & Fire at the Chase Center in San Francisco on Saturday night, at the United Center in Chicago on Sept, 30 and at the Schottenstein Center in Columbus, Ohio on Oct. 2. All three shows have been postponed with no makeup date immediately set, according to box office employees in San Francisco and Columbus and a statement by the United Center in Chicago. “Lionel underwent a common procedure for Atrial fibrillation (AFib),” a representative for Richie said in a statement. “The doctor said everything went perfectly. Lionel is doing great but will take some time off and will be back on stage soon.” Richie has a residency scheduled at the Encore Theater at Wynn Las Vegas, with shows set for Oct. 14, 16, 17 and Nov. 11, 13 and 14. A representative for the Las Vegas hotel and casino could not be immediately reached for comment on Tuesday. Richie has experienced troubling medical incidents in recent months. He was playing in St. Paul, Minnesota, on June 24 when he was forced to end the show early, telling fans he was feeling dizzy. He was performing “Dancing on the Ceiling” when he sat down on stage, stood up and walked a few feet before sitting down again. He also reportedly checked into a St. Louis hospital after feeling weak and dehydrated following an Aug. 29 show.

articles.title: A 17-year-old performed for a tiny crowd as if she were already famous. Then TikTok found her.
articles.summary: After a video of her performance unexpectedly took off, TikTok rallied around this 17-year-old's catchy hook and confidence.
articles.body:
For the last week, the surprise hit song "Vanessa Van D" has been playing in a loop in my head. And I'm not the only one. Creators have been posting their own videos dancing to the song .

The infectious bop comes from Vanessa Van Deusen, a 17-year-old singer-songwriter from small-town Carbondale, Pa., who suddenly has TikTok fanning out over her.

On Aug. 3, Van Deusen posted a video of herself performing her now-signature song at Lakeland Orchard & Cidery in the Scranton area. The setup was small-scale: a bandshell, a poster of herself on the wall and plastic Adirondack chairs for attendees. Yet Van Deusen treated it like the biggest stage in the world.

The video initially gained little traction. A few weeks later, TikTok's algorithm found it, turning it into For You Page fare.

"I fell asleep, and the video had, like, 30 likes," Van Deusen tells Yahoo. "I woke up and it had like 5,000. It just kept growing from there."

It now has over 2 million views. A second TikTok of Van Deusen singing the same name-checking earworm — also at a small venue while her two besties twirled batons — has racked up another 575,000 views.

"Yes, I am": TikTok discovers Van D's confidence

Social media videos go viral for all kinds of reasons. In this case, the Gen Z teen's earnestness — a bright spot in a sometimes cynical world — along with that catchy "Van D, Van D, Van D" hook turned viewers into instant fans.

You can practically watch it unfold in the comments on these two videos.

"Well, aren't you a confident little go-getter," one person wrote.

Van Deusen hopped into the comments with a sincerity that neutralized any potential shade: "Yes, I am," she replied.

When another person wrote, "AND THE CROWD GOES mild," she responded, "They're ✨admiring✨."

Others reached for pop-culture comparisons. " 'A Little Bit Alexis' walked so Vanessa Van D could run," one person wrote, referring to the memorable Schitt's Creek song. Rebecca Black's name came up too. Black was 13 when "Friday" went viral in 2011, and she became a target of widespread online ridicule.

But Van Deusen's comment section followed a different trajectory: The snark soon gave way to defense.

"Oh, let's make fun of the girl who took a risk and put herself out there creatively!!!!" someone wrote. That comment has about 2,000 likes.

Van Deusen, who manages her own TikTok, has felt the love from supporters.

"I posted a video a few days after the big one blew up, saying thank you for all your compliments and criticisms ," she says. "People were just rooting me on in the comments, being like, 'Who's being mean?' I have a fanbase now. They're so protective of me. That's when it really hit me: People actually want me to succeed."

Van Deusen's growing fandom already has nicknames, including the "Fan Ds" and the "Van Divas," she says.

The attention has brought opportunities for the teen. Brands have offered to send her products, Spotify has appeared in her comments and she has connected with the TikTok boy band Boy Throb.

So where did Van Deusen, who graduated high school in June, one year early, get the chutzpah not only to get onstage and be her own hype woman, but to let TikTok know she's unbothered? She's had practice.

Van Deusen began singing in middle school, an age when, as she puts it, "girls can be brutal." During those years, she says, classmates at her small private school bullied her.

"These girls were ruthless," she says. "They were bullying me every day. It got to a point where I'm like, 'Do I really want to do this?' And I'm like, 'You know what? Yeah.'"

She turned some of that hurt into music. One of her first songs, "Hey! (Are You a Lot Like Me)" was inspired by a friend who became a bully.

"Ever since then, I've had people criticize me," she says. "But I do know who my real friends are, and I'm forever grateful for them."

Van Deusen is currently unsigned but has been meeting with the same record label executive for about three years. Each time, he's given her a new assignment — first a ballad, then an anthem.

For the anthem assignment, she collaborated with her producer, "and that's how we got 'Van D,'" she says.

Even Van Deusen initially underestimated its appeal.

"When I first heard it, I was kind of iffy on it," she says. "It wasn't catching me yet. But a few days later, I was like, 'Oh my gosh, I can't get this out of my head,'" she says.

The timing of the song's viral rise couldn't have been better. Just days after the video took off, Van Deusen flew to Los Angeles on a previously planned trip to record more music.

"That just brought everyone along with me," she says, referring to how she shared behind-the-scenes footage on TikTok with her new followers. "It was amazing."

"I want to be up there with the legends"

Van Deusen has been performing since she was 2, starting with baton twirling and later adding singing and dancing. By high school, she was twirling fire.

Performance runs in the family. Her mother owns the twirling school where she trained, while her father once played in a band. At 17, Van Deusen, an only child, relies on her parents to help her navigate the industry.

"They've been the best at guiding me into the right decisions about where to go and what to do," she says. "I plan on keeping them on my team as I get older."

Now that she's found TikTok fame, it's full-speed ahead.

"I've wanted to be in the light since I was a little girl," she says. "With it becoming more and more apparent to me that this is a real thing — that this can happen, and now that it is happening — it propels me even more."

Van Deusen points to Taylor Swift and Sabrina Carpenter, two stars with Pennsylvania roots, as models for what might be possible beyond her hometown.

"I grew up [listening to] Taylor and Sabrina and have watched them grow and thrive," she says. "Knowing that they're as big as they are definitely influences me. [I think:] 'Yeah, I'm from a small town in Pennsylvania, but that doesn't stop me from going to Los Angeles or Nashville or New York.'"

Ultimately, she hopes other young performers will one day look at her the way she once looked at her idols.

"I want someone younger than me to say, 'Look, that's Vanessa Van D,' and be like, 'Wow, I want to be like her someday,'" Van Deusen says. "I want to be the next Taylor. I want to be the next Sabrina. I want to be up there with the legends."

For now, she's embracing where she is. Her next performance will be at Nay Aug Park in Scranton on Oct. 11, followed by a meet-and-greet.

articles.title: Sturgill Simpson says talent is 'not as rare as people think' and work ethic matters more
articles.summary: Sturgill Simpson ripped entitled singers with no work ethic, revealing what he says separates lasting careers from those flushed by the machine.
articles.body: Sturgill Simpson doesn't think there's a hidden secret to success in music. Simpson has carved out an incredibly loyal following in the country music industry by singing largely outlaw country tunes. However, that's far from his only skill. He also released a pair of albums under his alter ego Johnny Blue Skies. ‘YELLOWSTONE’ STAR LUKE GRIMES REVEALS OUTLAW COUNTRY WAS 'NO-GO' IN PASTOR FATHER’S HOUSE His secret to success? Just work hard. Sturgill Simpson blasts entitled and lazy singers. Simpson spoke with Playboy about his rise in the music industry, and he took some not-so-subtle shots at people who don't think they need to earn it. "I had all the thankless f***ing jobs. There are so many people I met when I moved to Nashville 15 years ago who had exponentially more talent than I do, but they had no work ethic. Or they thought [sic] that, because they were brilliant, they didn’t have to earn their medals," Simpson told Playboy (via Whiskey Riff). articles.title: Taylor Swift teases first new song after wedding, ‘Patient Zero’
articles.summary: Taylor Swift announced that she is releasing a new song titled “Patient Zero” at the end of the week.
articles.body: It’s a good day to be a Swiftie! On Sept. 22, Taylor Swift announced that she is releasing a new song titled “Patient Zero” at the end of the week. “I’ve been impatiently waiting to tell you that my brand new single ‘Patient Zero’ will be out on September 25 (!!!!!!!!!!!!)” the pop star wrote on her Instagram, alongside a new photo of herself. The single is currently available to pre-order on Swift’s website for 24 hours. The news comes after Swift has been leaving Easter eggs for fans the past two weeks, making Swifties question if the Grammy winner planned to announce new music. Swifties first speculated that Swift was up to something when she appeared in a skit at the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards on Sept. 14. During the sketch, which featured cast members from “Law & Order: Special Victims Unit,” Swift looked directly into the camera and said, “Saccharide. Aries. From the Vineyard. North or South.” Swifties immediately started to dissect the meaning, wondering if it pointed toward Swift releasing “Taylor’s Versions” of her debut and “Reputation” albums. For the past week, they have been sharing theories on social media. One X user posted a tweet that unscrambled the phrase to seemingly reveal a hidden message: “My first record’s re-record is out Nov. 10.” Then, fans noticed that a letter posted on Swift’s website in May 2025 confirming she purchased her master recordings suddenly had three pages instead of two. But theories linking the clues to her debut or “Reputation” albums started to lead to dead ends when zeroes began to appear in her song lyrics on Apple Music and Spotify. The final piece of the puzzle? Swift updated her Instagram bio to read, “And, baby, that’s sh0w business f0r y0u” the same day a countdown appeared on her website. All signs lead to “Patient Zero,” which will be Swift’s second release this year. In June, she announced the single “I Knew It, I Knew You,” from the “Toy Story 5” soundtrack. Swift did not confirm if “Patient Zero” will be the lead single from her highly-anticipated 13th album. Last year, she released “The Life of a Showgirl,” which included hits like “The Fate of Ophelia,” “Opalite” and “Elizabeth Taylor.” Her 12th album broke a record with its first week sales, selling over 4 million units.

articles.body: Este martes 'La Revuelta' ha vuelto un día más a la franja horaria del 'access prime time' de La 1 de RTVE. En esta ocasión, la invitada que ha pasado por el Teatro Albéniz de Madrid ha sido una de las cantantes de nuestro país con mayor trayectoria, Malú, quien ha presentado su gira 'Quince Tour'. Lo primero que ha preguntado David Broncano a la invitada ha sido cuándo fue la última vez que fue a una fiesta electrónica hasta las siete de la mañana. “No he ido nunca, no me ha dado tiempo y no podía entrar. A los 18 yo ya estaba trabajando y tenía que cuidar la voz”, ha contestado Malú en la que ha sido su primera visita a 'La Revuelta'. Después de estas palabras, Malú ha destacado que su nuevo proyecto profesional es especial porque repasa los temas más destacados de sus casi tres décadas sobre los escenarios. No obstante, ha manifestado que la discográfica no le dejó elegir el nombre del disco. "Se me ocurrieron tres muy currados, para mí eran genialidades, pero los lanzaba y al equipo no le gustaban", ha apuntado. “Me dijeron: ahora te has pasado de fácil. Pero empecé a los 15, nací un día 15, llevo 15 discos y 30 años, 15+15, así que lo dejé así”, ha continuado la cantante, asegurando que terminó quedándose con el nombre de 'Quince'. Por último, Malú no ha eludido las preguntas clásicas del programa y ha dejado totalmente descolocado a David Broncano, sobre todo con lo referente a la cuestión del sexo. "Todo el rato. Llego tarde a los conciertos porque no quiero parar. Aprovecho hasta en los cambios de ropa", ha asegurado la artista madrileña. El cómico jienense no se lo ha podido creer, por lo que le ha pedido una cifra aproximada de relaciones sexuales en el último mes. "Cien", ha respondido la invitada entre risas. "Necesitaría una auditoría", ha sentenciado el presentador de 'La Revuelta' siguiendo la broma.

articles.title: Javier Bardem slammed for targeting Pink over Macklemore comments: 'The left is eating itself'
articles.summary: Actor Javier Bardem promoted a petition to remove Pink as a UNICEF ambassador, drawing fierce pushback from Michael Rapaport and Selma Blair.
articles.body: Actor Javier Bardem has stepped into the middle of the controversy surrounding Pink, Macklemore and the Israel-Gaza conflict — and is now taking heat for it. The "No Country for Old Men" star shared multiple posts to his Instagram Stories Monday urging followers to sign a Change.org petition demanding that Pink be removed as a UNICEF ambassador, according to Reuters. The petition Bardem promoted, titled "Remove Pink as a UNICEF Ambassador," calls on the organization to remove the singer from her position. ED SHEERAN SAYS HE TRIED TO ‘BUILD A BRIDGE’ OVER MACKLEMORE TOUR SPOT BEFORE VENUES SAID NO Supporters argue that Pink’s comments are "incompatible with the role of a UNICEF Ambassador" and say ambassadors should promote "peace, understanding, and humanitarian values above personal biases." The petition urges UNICEF to "take decisive action and remove Pink as an ambassador," arguing that the organization must remain committed to all children regardless of "nationality or heritage." Bardem’s move drew pushback from fans and fellow celebrities who questioned why the actor was backing an effort to strip Pink of her UNICEF title over comments she made after Macklemore’s pro-Palestinian concert appearance. Michael Rapaport delivered one of the most blistering responses, mocking Bardem as a "tattletale" and accusing the actor of going after Pink through a petition rather than confronting her directly. He wrote in an Instagram caption: "Javier Bar-Dumb Dumb initiated,signed & is promoting a petition to have singer PINK removed as a UNICEF Ambassador. He’s is Bullying a Proud Jewish Woman." Rapaport continued in his video: "Javier Bar-Dumb Dumb. Javier Bardem, what the f--- are you doing, you little tattle-tale? Hall monitor … you are a grown man, a grown f---ing man. Pink is a grown woman. You're both world-famous. If you have a problem with what she said, call her. Sit her down, have a coffee, look her dead in the face and express all and any frustrations and questions you have … instead you sign a petition, like a little b---- to have her removed as a UNICEF ambassador. What the f--- is wrong with you?" PINK HITS BACK AMID BACKLASH FOR CRITICIZING MACKLEMORE'S PRO-PALESTINIAN CONCERT REMARKS Selma Blair also weighed in in the comment section, writing: "Why would anyone want this great removed from unicef for human , humble and loving words? This makes no sense. I would think the terrifically talented actor man would worry about his own incredible life more. And allow love to flow. And listen to everybody. Not just his echo chamber. But alas." Bardem's decision to promote the petition also drew criticism from social media users, with commenters questioning why the actor was pushing for Pink's removal over her comments. One commenter wrote: "I'm not a big Pink fan...I like her music okay, but she was one of the many performers who actually did ads for Big Pharma pushing the vax during covid. That said, who the hell is Bardem to cancel her? The left is eating itself." Meanwhile, supporters of Bardem's position also commented on the petition. "Pink chose her and her rich friends' discomfort was more important than people's lives," one commenter wrote, adding that if UNICEF does not "stand with Gaza now and remove Pink," then "the world is a much darker place." Another argued, "No ambassador can call attention to important issues while actively ignoring and deliberately misunderstanding and misrepresenting the conditions in Palestine. Pink has shown herself incapable of even acknowledging what is clear to the world, and is not fit to serve UNICEF." A third commenter questioned how Pink could remain a UNICEF advocate while, in their view, failing to support "basic human rights and free speech for all people, especially those in Gaza, the Sudan and the Congo." Fox News Digital reached out to Bardem, UNICEF and Pink for comment. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS MACKLEMORE DONATES $1M TO PALESTINIAN AID ORGANIZATIONS AFTER ED SHEERAN TOUR FALLOUT The petition Bardem promoted centers on Pink’s response to Macklemore’s appearance with Ed Sheeran at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, on Sept. 4. Macklemore performed "Hind's Hall," his song supporting Palestinians, while repeatedly chanting "Free Palestine" as images related to Gaza appeared on a screen behind him. The performance sparked criticism from the @Stop_Antisemitism Instagram account, which accused Macklemore of using the concert to push "anti-Israel propaganda." Pink faced backlash after reposting the criticism and subsequently issued her own lengthy explanation. "I’ve been quiet in my own words for a week, which you know isn’t like me. So here they are," she wrote on social media. "I was born a Jew," Pink continued. "I didn’t pick it, and I’ve never hidden it." GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE She also addressed her position on the conflict. "Of course I don’t speak for Israel, or for any government. I never have," Pink wrote. "What I said in October 2023 is still exactly what I believe: Hamas is a terrorist organization. Palestinians deserve a future that honors their humanity and their aspirations. Protecting innocent life comes first, everywhere, and nobody should ever celebrate the death of a child. Anybody’s child." Pink also cited her years of work with UNICEF, saying she had spent time with children "on both sides of that fence." "I’m not going to litigate a complex war in an Instagram caption, and I’m not going to recite anybody’s slogan to earn back a follower," she wrote. Pink went on to explain that what she was "reacting to" was Macklemore himself. She recalled him performing his song "Same Love" at the Grammys in 2014, and how she cheered on the message, but "Four months later Macklemore put on a hooked nose, a black beard and a bowl cut, performed in it, and called it a 'random costume.'" "Every Jew I know knew exactly what it was. The same love, it turned out, had a guest list, and we weren’t on it. But he apologized, and I let it go, because that’s what we do. We let it go. Then last weekend he stood in front of a stadium full of music-loving families, with violent images from a war on the screens, dedicated a song to the movement of his choice, and then took the mic to tell all of the Jews in the stadium that it wasn’t about them." She added, "You don’t get to decide that for us." "That’s what prompted my repost," she wrote. "Not 'Free Palestine,' and not anyone’s right to say it. What I need is to be able to say, as a Jewish mom, 'that scared me, and it scared people I love,' without being told our fear is just propaganda, and without being told I’m somehow cool with genocide because I noticed?" Macklemore later posted a video on Instagram addressing the crowd and said performing on Sheeran's tour gave him the opportunity to deliver his "Free Palestine" message to a massive audience. articles.title: Mahershala Ali Agrees That Kevin Feige Is a 'Gigantic Loser and Failure' Over Failed Blade Reboot
articles.summary: Oscar-winning actor Mahershala Ali wholeheartedly agreed with Kevin Feige’s description of himself as a “gigantic loser and failure” for not getting Marvel Studios’ Blade reboot off the ground.
articles.body:
Oscar-winning actor Mahershala Ali wholeheartedly agreed with Kevin Feige’s description of himself as a “gigantic loser and failure” for not getting Marvel Studios’ canceled Blade reboot off the ground.

Feige made the remark on an episode of Josh Horowitz’s Happy Sad Confused podcast in late July, where he spoke about how excited he was to have Wesley Snipes reprise the role of Blade on Deadpool & Wolverine — an emotion that contrasted sharply with his failed attempts at making Ali’s reboot happen.

It turns out that Ali feels the same way. The actor admitted as much during a September 22 chat with GQ's Zach Baron , who cautiously broached the subject to see how Ali felt about the project now that it’s firmly in his rear view.

Who Is Blade? Marvel’s Vampire Hunter Explained

“That’s a Kevin Feige question,” he responded when asked why the film never moved forward. “They had, as you said, a two-time Oscar-winning actor under contract, and you got billions of dollars. …To this day, I don’t know why it didn’t happen. I just know that Kevin said it was the biggest failure of his career, and I agree.”

“I believe the quote was, ‘I feel like a giant loser and a failure,’” Baron suggested.

“I agree with him, one hundred percent. He should feel that way,” Ali continued.

Ali’s brutally honest remarks have gone viral online, and it’s not hard to see why; in that same interview, the actor freely admitted that he’d spent a year of his life in physical training to convincingly portray Marvel’s Daywalker, and worked out so hard that he literally blew out his knee.

“I was waiting for them… [they were] pushing it back, pushing it back. I’m still training, I'm learning swordwork. Name a martial art, I’m training in it. I literally moved, uprooted my family, moved to Atlanta. We were there waiting to go, and they just kept pushing it back,” he explained.

Ali first met with Marvel all the way back in 2019. It’s been seven years since then, and despite having a story greenlit and costumes made, the film never came to fruition. Some of those costumes were later used on the Academy Award-winning movie Sinners , while Ali said that much of the combat skills he learned while preparing for Blade were put to use in his newest film, Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother .

With Ali no longer attached and a stigma surrounding the failed Blade reboot, it’s looking less likely than ever that we’ll get to see Blade take on a new adventure — and that really sucks, because Ali was the perfect fit to play the part.

articles.title: CNN staffers accept new reality as Paramount's takeover of Warner Bros Discovery goes full steam ahead
articles.summary: CNN staffers reveal mixed emotions as Paramount's merger with Warner Bros. Discovery moves forward following the settlement with State Attorneys General.
articles.body: A new reality is setting in for CNN's rank and file as the network will once again have new ownership following Paramount's merger with its parent company, Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD). "I think people are like, 'Let's just get this done,'" one CNN staffer told Fox News Digital. Paramount's $111 billion bid to buy WBD overcame its biggest obstacle, which was the antitrust lawsuit spearheaded by California Attorney General Rob Bonta and several other Democratic State AGs. Instead of battling it out in court during the March 2027 trial date, both parties reached a settlement Monday, paving the way for Paramount CEO David Ellison to take the reins of two legacy Hollywood studios and two major news organizations — CNN and CBS News — among other assets. Negotiated in the settlement is the implementation of an independent editorial board that will oversee both news outlets. PARAMOUNT REACHES SETTLEMENT WITH STATES SUING TO BLOCK WARNER BROS DISCOVERY MERGER There have been several reports of internal strife within the CNN newsroom since the settlement was reached, but at least one network staffer believes the sentiment is more nuanced based on conversations they've had with colleagues. "I think there are fewer people internally opposed to the merger than there used to be," the CNN staffer said. "People internally just want direction." A second CNN staffer disagreed with the notion that they aren't personally opposed to the merger, telling Fox News Digital, "Nothing has changed about anyone's views at CNN." "If there is that perception, it is coming from the fact that this has been out there for a long time so people are less loud. That shouldn’t be confused with a change of mindset," they said. CNN STAFFERS BRACE FOR PARAMOUNT CEO'S POTENTIAL PLAN TO LAUNCH EDITORIAL BOARD TO OVERSEE NETWORK A lot of unknowns loom over CNN as the merger proceeds. First are the company wide layoffs that are expected to take place that will likely impact CNN. Second is the change in CNN's leadership — whether its current CEO Mark Thompson will remain or whether Ellison's appointed CBS News editor-in-chief Bari Weiss will have a new role overseeing both news operations, as reports previously suggested. "I don’t know who will run CNN," the second staffer said. "Ellison will have a lot of pressure to make that decision and not to say let Mark Thompson stay on for a little while to not deal with it or fake anybody out. It’s better for his business to make a clean, strong decision and let everybody know." While they're glad the Paramount merger brings clarity about the network's future, the CNN insider is dreading "fairly dramatic" cuts that will ultimately rock the newsroom. "CNN will be diminished," the second staffer said. "However, that is already happening macro and micro to us and all other legacy media." Representatives for CNN and Paramount declined to comment. FORMER '60 MINUTES' HONCHO SAYS CBS NEWS LEADERS WANTED STAFF TO 'COMPROMISE OUR PRINCIPLES' Much of the opposition toward the Paramount-WBD merger stemmed from Ellison's taking control over CNN. Liberal critics claimed that as a result of the deal, CNN would be given a MAGA-bent to its coverage, pointing to Ellison and his billionaire father Larry Ellison's cozy relationship with President Donald Trump, and worried Ellison's CNN would be run by CBS News chief Bari Weiss, who has been ostracized by the far-left despite her outspoken left-of-center politics. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Ellison has previously assured that CNN would maintain editorial independence following the merger. In a guest essay published in The New York Times, the Paramount CEO addressed the "speculation" about what would happen to CNN under his ownership. "I have regularly voted for candidates of both parties; I hold some views that would be called conservative and others that would be called liberal, just like most Americans; and when it comes to our news operations, I do not aspire to lead these companies to bend their newsrooms to my views. I believe that news should be based on facts and truth," Ellison wrote. "Great news organizations like CNN and CBS News are here to tell it straight down the middle," he added. "That requires newsrooms that reflect the whole world, not one side of it. And it requires independence."

articles.title: She wrote ‘Killing Me Softly’ on a napkin in 1971. It took decades for her to get the credit.
articles.summary: Folk singer Lori Lieberman's heartfelt reaction to a Don McLean concert inspired a classic, but her contributions were underplayed.
articles.body:
Lori Lieberman wrote the original version of "Killing Me Softly" on a napkin in 1971 after being inspired by a Don McLean concert at the Troubadour.

Roberta Flack's 1973 rendition of "Killing Me Softly" became a massive hit, earning three Grammy Awards and a spot on Rolling Stone's list of the greatest songs of all time.

Despite being the inspiration behind the song, Lori Lieberman spent years being minimized in the story until Don McLean publicly backed her account and set the record straight.

Some songs feel like they've always been a part of us. No matter how long they've been around, they feel like timeless tunes woven into the fabric of our lives. One could argue that "Killing Me Softly (With His Song)" is one such song.

You've undoubtedly heard Roberta Flack's soulful, intimate 1973 version. It peaked at #1 around the world and became a staple of that decade's soul-infused hits. In 1996, Lauren Hill's version with The Fugees introduced a new generation to the song, layering in a hip-hop beat sampled from A Tribe Called Quest's "Bonita Applebaum."

What most people don't know is that both of these versions are covers. The song's origins began with one young woman's raw, emotional reaction to a concert she attended on a whim and a poem she scribbled on a napkin in the dark.

A night at the Troubadour changed everything

In November 1971, a 19-year-old singer named Lori Lieberman let a friend talk her into catching a show at LA's famous Troubadour club. Headlining the night was "American Pie" singer Don McLean. During his performance, something shifted in Lieberman. She began connecting not only with the music but with the emotions McLean's melodies and lyrics evoked. Lieberman grabbed a napkin and scribbled down her feelings , letting them spill out in real time.

Soon after, Lieberman shared that tear-stained poem with songwriters Norman Gimbel and Charles Fox. The pair were producing and writing material for her debut album. Gimbel crafted the lyric, "Killing me softly with his blues." But as they wrote the song, they adapted it to fit the track's folk-inspired tone.

Lieberman recorded the song in 1972. It barely made a ripple. A year later, Roberta Flack heard the song playing on an airplane's in-flight music channel . At producer Quincy Jones's encouragement, Flack laid down her own version. A year later, her rendition crossed over to multiple Billboard charts and became a massive hit. Eventually, it earned three Grammy Awards , including Song of the Year. Not only is it a '70s soul classic, but it also ranks #273 on Rolling Stone 's "The 500 Greatest Songs of All Time" list.

For decades, the woman who inspired it all got pushed out of the story

Despite being the catalyst for "Killing Me Softly," Lieberman spent years watching her contribution get minimized. Gimbel and Fox, who held the official songwriting credit, began distancing themselves from the origin story. For Lieberman, it was a strange kind of erasure. She was being written out of a story that was, quite literally, from her own life.

The person who ultimately helped set the record straight was Don McLean himself—the very artist whose performance had given Lieberman her inspiration. He publicly backed Lieberman's account on his now-shuttered personal website. He even tracked down a 1973 Daily News article where Gimbel himself tells the story of Lieberman's concert experience.

Lieberman has never chased royalties or sought official credit. She's only wanted simple acknowledgment of her real, lived experience: a night at a local club where a performer's voice and music electrified her. His songs made her feel seen, and that moment became the seed of one of pop music's most enduring standards, first scribbled on a tear-stained napkin.

articles.title: Paramount will need to release way more movies to make this merger work
articles.summary: Paramount’s promise to release more films annually after merging with Warner Bros. Discovery may be very difficult to keep.
articles.body: Now that Paramount has reached a settlement with the 12 states that were suing to block its $110 billion merger with Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD), the studio is even closer to becoming one of the world’s biggest production houses. In addition to spending at least $300 million more on film and TV projects produced in the US, Paramount says that it will release a minimum of 30 movies annually after it absorbs WBD. On paper, these goals make it sound like Paramount is trying to ensure that the entertainment industry won’t be harmed by its WBD acquisition. But when you look at the studios’ recent output, it seems very much like Paramount CEO David Ellison is making promises to the public that he might not be able to keep. In a statement about the settlement, California Attorney General Rob Bonta stressed that the settlement was designed to maintain consistent film output and domestic production while “protecting the livelihoods of workers above and below the line.” (Of course, any redundancies caused by a merger of this scale will likely lead to layoffs, which makes Bonta’s claim that the settlement “protects workers, jobs, and Hollywood” questionable in the first place.) In a statement of their own, Screen Actors Guild – American Federation of Television and Radio Artists (SAG-AFTRA) president Sean Astin and chief negotiator Duncan Crabtree-Ireland thanked Bonta and noted that the settlement represents “the lowest standards that our employers must meet.” Though the acquisition — which has not yet officially been finalized — would permanently fuse Paramount and WBD, the settlement only requires the newly merged company to adhere to a few rules for just five years. In the first two years, Paramount/WBD has to either put out 30 films annually or pay $30 million per film into healthcare and retirement funds managed by Hollywood’s biggest unions. During the following three years, the merged studio would need to release 32 films annually, and if it fails to meet any of these requirements during this five-year period, it will be forced to sell off its 49 percent stake in Miramax Studios to one of its competitors. [Image: In terms of overall output, these proposed goals would be a step up for both Paramount and WBD as separate corporate entities. Over the past six years (including projects slated to debut later in 2026), Paramount has released an average of 15 films annually while WBD has averaged 17. Assuming that the newly merged studio will stick to Paramount and WBD’s previously announced release slates for 2027 and 2028, it would need to put more than a few new projects on the board in order to avoid multimillion dollar penalties. But that probably isn’t all that much of a concern to Paramount because the settlement doesn’t require the new company to produce the projects necessary to hit its annual movie quota. Paramount/WBD could fulfill its obligations by distributing films that it acquires from other production houses. These films would carry the Paramount/WBD branding, but they would be the products of labor carried out by teams with no direct connection to the studio. Paramount/WBD could also flood the zone with completely new, original films it greenlights and finances itself. But many of those movies could feel less ambitious because the settlement only requires that 20 percent of them have production budgets over $50 million. Paramount appears to have convinced Bonta and his fellow attorneys general that absorbing WBD will give it the ability to basically double its usual output. But that logic presumes every single aspect of both studios’ production pipelines will continue to operate normally once Paramount and WBD become one. Though Paramount/WBD could ramp internal production up, what feels much more likely to happen is the studio doing the bare minimum to abide by the settlement’s terms. articles.title: Azeite da Serra da Mantiqueira conquista prêmio internacional: ‘Estou me sentindo ganhando um Oscar’, diz produtor | G1
articles.standfirst: Fazenda em Santo Antônio do Pinhal foi premiada no Flos Olei 2026, guia internacional especializado em azeites extravirgens.
articles.summary: Fazenda em Santo Antônio do Pinhal foi premiada no Flos Olei 2026, guia internacional especializado em azeites extravirgens.
articles.body:
‘Oscar’ dos azeites: produto da Serra da Mantiqueira, no interior de SP, vence prêmio mundial com variedade espanhola — Foto: Reprodução/Ana Beloto

Um azeite produzido na Serra da Mantiqueira, no interior de São Paulo, conquistou um dos principais reconhecimentos internacionais do setor. Uma fazenda em Santo Antônio do Pinhal foi premiada no Flos Olei 2026, guia internacional especializado em azeites extravirgens.

A propriedade venceu na categoria “The Best Extra Virgin Olive Oil – Extraction System”, que reconhece o melhor sistema de extração, e na categoria de Melhor Azeite Extravirgem na variedade Picual. O empresário e produtor de azeites Sabiá, João Roberto “Bob” Vieira da Costa, compara o reconhecimento a um “Oscar” do setor.

“Estou me sentindo ganhando um Oscar. É um Oscar do mundo dos azeites”, afirmou Bob ao g1.

O produtor está também concorrendo na Flos Olei de 2027, novamente como "The Best Extra Virgin Olive Oil - Extraction System".

O Flos Olei, sediado na Itália, reúne produtores de azeite extravirgem de 57 países e cinco continentes. A publicação apresenta os 500 produtores classificados no guia e distribui diferentes categorias de premiação.

A qualidade do azeite, segundo Bob, começa com o acompanhamento do ponto de maturação da azeitona. Depois da colheita, a fruta precisa ser levada rapidamente para ser processada.

Na fazenda, a equipe chegou a trocar o equipamento de extração para reduzir o intervalo entre a colheita e o processamento. A azeitona passa por lavagem, moagem, mistura e centrifugação até a separação do azeite. Depois, o produto é filtrado e armazenado em tanques de aço inox.

O controle da temperatura também é considerado fundamental para preservar a qualidade do produto.

A fazenda também adotou uma metodologia de degustação durante o processo de produção. Um grupo avalia o azeite antes da filtragem e pode indicar ajustes, como no tempo de mistura ou na velocidade de moagem.

“Cada dia é um azeite diferente”, explicou Bob, destacando que fatores como chuva, umidade e estágio de maturação da fruta podem interferir no resultado.

Além dos pratos salgados, a Fazenda Sabiá também apresenta aos visitantes combinações menos convencionais, como azeite sobre sorvete.

Segundo Bob, a experiência costuma surpreender quem experimenta pela primeira vez. A propriedade oferece degustações em Santo Antônio do Pinhal, com visita ao processo de produção e provas de diferentes tipos de azeite.

articles.title: Karol G exalta funk e revela sonho de romper barreira musical no Brasil: 'Tem sido um processo' | G1
articles.standfirst: Em coletiva de imprensa, artista colombiana falou sobre influência da cultura brasileira no show da 'Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour', que passa por São Paulo em fevereiro.
articles.summary: Em coletiva de imprensa, artista colombiana falou sobre influência da cultura brasileira no show da 'Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour', que passa por São Paulo em fevereiro.
articles.body:
Karol G vem coroando um grande momento na carreira neste ano. A cantora colombiana conquistou o topo do Spotify global (com a música "Bby Wow"), foi indicada a sete prêmios no Grammy Latino e lançou parcerias com Drake e Bruno Mars. Ela também está enchendo estádios com a sua turnê atual, a "Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour", que passa pelo Brasil em fevereiro.

O g1 assistiu ao show da cantora no Metlife Stadium, em Nova York, no dia 17 de setembro. Foi a primeira de duas apresentações na cidade, com 53 mil ingressos esgotados por noite e um público totalmente entregue.

Ao longo do megashow, Karol reúne elementos musicais, culturais e visuais latinos, com direito a muito Brasil: da versão de "Tá Ok" a referências ao Carnaval e vários momentos de funk. Tudo isso tem um objetivo — em coletiva de imprensa, a artista explicou que a cultura brasileira a fascina, e que ela está mirando em se aproximar do Brasil.

"Eu queria garantir que tivesse um pedacinho da América Latina em cada música, e o Brasil tem uma magia incrível para mim. O funk me fascina, a música sertaneja me encanta demais, ouço muito. Consigo encontrar minhas formas de ir me aproximando cada vez um pouquinho mais, e o Brasil não fica de fora".

Karol G em show no Metlife Stadium, em Nova York, no dia 17 de setembro de 2026 — Foto: Divulgação/Henry Hwu

Nos momentos mais calientes (e um ponto alto) do show, Karol inclui mesclas de funk e reggaeton em um segundo palco, transformado em "piscina".

Ela explica que vê o funk como uma ferramenta de empoderamento e sensualidade: "O funk me dá muita alegria, me faz sentir linda, me faz sentir sexy, me faz sentir que danço de forma impressionante. Tudo me fascina, o quadradinho, uau, as 'mamacitas'...".

Ainda que Karol pareça ter o público latino na palma da mão, o Brasil ainda é um território que ela não conquistou por inteiro. É o velho desafio para artistas que cantam em espanhol: furar a bolha de um país que é uma espécie de ilha musical e raramente se abre para outros idiomas.

Na coletiva, Karol explicou que romper essa barreira "sempre foi um sonho" em sua carreira.

"Gosto muitíssimo da cultura de vocês e gosto muito de como são as cores e os matizes que vocês têm. Eu tive a oportunidade de ir ao Brasil em carnavais, em festas (...) e é de fato o significado de festa, alegria. Ninguém está atento a ninguém, todo mundo está em si mesmo, as pessoas estão como em uma energia espetacular", disse.

"Sinto que o Brasil é como um planeta, é como o seu próprio universo, e vocês aí desfrutam o que acontece no Brasil, a música brasileira sempre é a mais ouvida. Sempre foi um sonho romper essa barreira e ter a oportunidade de entrar em um lugar que me causa tanta graça e que eu gosto tanto. Tem sido um processo entrar no Brasil. Acho que ainda não tive uma música que esteja no top ou algo assim, mas tive a oportunidade de cantar com artistas daí, de me conectar com artistas daí e eu amo... vejo meu show como uma oportunidade de continuar conquistando corações".

Karol G em show no Metlife Stadium, em Nova York, no dia 17 de setembro de 2026 — Foto: Divulgação/Baeth

"Eu nunca dou nada por garantido e, de fato, o mundo é tão grande que posso dizer que estou em uma porcentagem muito pequena do que eu gostaria que a minha música ainda vai alcançar. Então, tudo isso e a ideia de fazer sempre com que tudo o que façamos seja com muita excelência, aproveitar cada oportunidade que temos para continuar chegando a mais e mais pessoas. Mais do que esperar algo de antemão, espero que depois do show se consolide um pouquinho mais essa nossa relação com os brasileiros. Essa é a minha ilusão".

Como parte desse investimento no país, a cantora garante que o show no Brasil terá várias surpresas.

"De certa forma vamos conseguir que, quando estivermos no Brasil, esse universo esteja ainda mais presente. Por isso, não consigo me conter. Espero que você venha para notar as diferenças que há entre o que estamos fazendo versus o que vamos fazer no Brasil, mas é super especial. Trouxemos um pedacinho dessa música urbana do Brasil que eu gosto tanto".

Karol G durante show no Metlife Stadium, em Nova York, no dia 17 de setembro — Foto: Divulgação/Henry Hwu

articles.summary: Ella Langley celebrated a career-defining milestone after “Choosin’ Texas" spent its 23rd week at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100.
articles.body: Ella Langley knew "Choosin' Texas" was special. Even she couldn't have predicted just how far it would go. On Tuesday night, Langley took to Instagram to celebrate making Billboard Hot 100 history this week when "Choosin' Texas" logged its 23rd week at No. 1, surpassing Mariah Carey's "All I Want for Christmas Is You" for the longest reign at the top of the chart. "I'm genuinely trying to find the words to explain what's going on in my brain today," Langley began her video. "What? I don't know. Thank you so much. Thank you for loving this song, for listening to it. I feel like… I just don't even know what to say at this point. I'm running out of hyperboles to describe how I feel, so I will just let my dog in the background show you his excitement," she continued as her dog barked. "Just thank you. Thank you so much. It's changing my life. It's changing the lives of the writers of this song. It's changing the lives of my family and it is truly growing an atmosphere for something I'm gonna be able to do the rest of my life and I just… today doesn't feel like a real thing," Langley said. "It feels fake and somebody's going to come in and be like 'haha we're kidding the whole time just kidding.'" ELLA LANGLEY SEEMINGLY FIRES BACK AFTER DOJA CAT'S BRUTAL TAKE ON HER CHART-TOPPING HIT "I'm really excited to just experience a moment like this in my life," she said. The country music star told her fans that she was going to celebrate tonight before ending with, "Choosin' T… that's the one huh?" In a resurfaced interview with Billboard from March, when the song was still climbing, Langley admitted its success had already surpassed anything she imagined when she wrote it. "When we wrote it, I knew it was going on the record. I honestly knew it was going to be the lead single," Langley told Billboard. "And we love that song, but I don't think I could have ever imagined what's happening with it right now," she continued. "Like I said, every day I wake up and it's doing something that I didn't even know was a goal that I could have had." "It's just nuts," Langley added. "It's crazy to see the ownership that the fans have taken over it. And the different demographics of people listening to the song is so cool." What seemed unimaginable to Langley in March has since become historic. ELLA LANGLEY'S 'CHOOSIN' TEXAS' SPENDS 15 WEEKS AT NUMBER ONE ON THE BILLBOARD HOT 100 "Choosin' Texas" first entered the Hot 100 in November 2025, became Langley's first top 10 in January and reached No. 1 for the first time in February. The song has also spent 41 weeks at No. 1 on Billboard's Hot Country Songs chart. Long before it became a record breaker, however, "Choosin' Texas" began with a story about a kangaroo. Langley recalled writing the song during her first songwriting retreat with country superstar Miranda Lambert and two other writers. "So, I was on a writer's retreat with Miranda," Langley explained in the resurfaced Billboard interview. "This is our first time that we had written together and obviously we were there with two others." Langley said Lambert began telling her a story about a pet kangaroo. "I learned at a young age she had a pet kangaroo and I wanted to ask her about it," Langley recalled. "So, I was like, 'Tell me about this kangaroo that you had. I need to know.'" ELLA LANGLEY'S TEXAS PHOTO DUMP SENDS COUNTRY MUSIC FANS INTO A FRENZY ONLINE ON INSTAGRAM Lambert told the group about once being pulled over with the kangaroo riding in the passenger seat and a dog in the back. Advertisment "She said she got pulled over and the kangaroo ended up getting her out of a ticket, but she's like, 'Of course, I had Texas plates on, too,'" Langley recalled. ELLA LANGLEY JOINS MUSIC ROYALTY WITH 'INSANE' MILESTONE FOR 'CHOOSIN' TEXAS' That was enough to spark the song. "And I went, 'Well, she's from Texas, I can tell,'" Langley said. "And just from that phrase, it kind of all hit us." According to Langley, the melody came almost immediately, with Lambert helping develop the story behind it. "And 45 minutes later, we had that song written," Langley said. "And it was just, it was such a cool experience." Lambert's involvement didn't end in the writing room. Langley told Billboard that the country superstar was executive producing her next record and had become someone she could turn to for advice. "There's not a rulebook to this job," Langley said. "How crazy is that?" Langley said. "And for me, like, what, me? You mean me?" Six months later, "Choosin' Texas" stands alone as the longest-running No. 1 song in Hot 100 history. articles.title: Jordi Roca, chef con tres estrellas: "Para que el pollo asado quede jugoso por dentro, siéntalo sobre una cerveza"
articles.standfirst: El cocinero de El Celler de Can Roca propone una curiosa técnica para preparar pollo al horno con la carne jugosa y la piel dorada y crujiente
articles.summary: El cocinero de El Celler de Can Roca propone una curiosa técnica para preparar pollo al horno con la carne jugosa y la piel dorada y crujiente
articles.body: Conseguir que un pollo asado quede jugoso por dentro y dorado por fuera puede ser más complicado de lo que parece. Unos minutos de más en el horno pueden terminar dejando la carne seca, especialmente en la zona de la pechuga. Jordi Roca propone una solución tan sencilla como llamativa: sentar el pollo sobre una cerveza. "Si quieres que el pollo asado quede jugoso por dentro, debes sentarlo sobre una cerveza", explica el cocinero en una receta que ha compartido y que posteriormente ha sido recogida por diferentes medios gastronómicos. Jordi Roca, responsable de la parte dulce de El Celler de Can Roca, ha incluido esta preparación en su libro 'Cosas de casa'. La receta parte de una técnica conocida como 'pollo sentado', pero el chef introduce su propia combinación de especias y utiliza un vaso o recipiente con cerveza. La preparación comienza calentando el horno a 180 grados. Mientras tanto, se prepara una mezcla con pimentón dulce, pimentón picante, mostaza en polvo, azúcar moreno, especias para pollo asado, tomillo y sal. El pollo entero se masajea con aceite de oliva y después se cubre con la mezcla de especias para que quede bien impregnado por toda su superficie. El paso más llamativo llega entonces. En lugar de colocar el pollo tumbado sobre la bandeja, Roca propone introducir un vaso cilíndrico resistente al calor, con cerveza en su interior, en la cavidad del pollo y colocarlo de forma vertical, de manera que el ave quede literalmente "sentada". El pollo se coloca encima y se hornea durante aproximadamente una hora 180 grados, hasta que adquiere un tono dorado. La idea detrás de esta técnica es que la cerveza se vaya calentando durante la cocción y genere vapor en el interior del pollo. De esta forma, se busca mantener la humedad de la carne mientras el exterior recibe el calor necesario para conseguir una piel dorada y crujiente.

articles.title: How does Norwich University of the Arts stand out from its peers?
articles.summary: Recent graduate Janet Chase says the university has unlocked many doors and opportunities.
articles.body:
Students at an arts university have shared why they felt it deserved to be named as the best of its kind in the UK.

Norwich University of the Arts (NUA) has been picked as the specialist university of the year in The Times and The Sunday Times' Good University Guide 2027, months after the newspaper revealed the city as the best place to live in the UK.

Janet Chase, 61, who has just graduated from a four-year fine art degree, said she felt the university had unlocked many doors to her as a mature student.

"I can't tell you how I entered feeling quite nervous, and [I'm] exiting feeling rounded and my confidence has grown enormously," she said.

Founded in 1845 by artists and followers of the Norwich School of Painters, the university now offers courses across art, architecture, design, fashion, communication, performing arts, business, marketing and psychology.

Chase, who is NUA's Students' Union president of education and representation, has just finished a month-long residency in Finland.

"I had a sadness in my life and I wanted to change it... I didn't realise I could do a degree and the rest is history," she said.

"To be a president of this university as a mature student is what everyone can do if they want, so I advocate everything 'mature' at this university.

"My four years here have been unbelievable - there are opportunities out there for mature students."

Last year, the university invested in a new virtual production studio in partnership with two technology firms.

The video wall , based in the city's Mile Cross district, creates the illusion of actors, creators or newsreaders being in any location imaginable.

NUA hoped it would help put it at the forefront of the next generation of film-making in the UK.

Earlier this year, it was announced the university had joined forces with the Royal College of Art (RCA) to offer jointly awarded undergraduate courses at the Norwich campus from next September.

Vice Chancellor Prof Ben Stopher said the newspaper award rewarded the institution's hard work.

He said: "The focus of it is so much on student learning and academic excellence, and that's what's really driving the award.

"To get that recognition is a great moment for us."

Student Trinity Drummond, 20 and originally from Surrey, is learning game art design and said she was keen to encourage more people to study gaming in the city.

Drummond, who is also Students' Union president of community and welfare, said: "The course was the best course I could find anywhere - and especially with the Royal College of Art - I think it's going to get so much better and bigger.

"It's already so amazing, so I can't even imagine how much more amazing it's going to be."

The city's University of East Anglia (UEA) also received recognition across a number of subject areas in the latest Good University Guide, with nine subjects ranked in the top 15.

Four subjects, including social work, anthropology, physiotherapy and nursing, secured spots in the top 10.

Stopher said both of the universities strived to help strengthen the city's reputation.

"We've worked for years to really try and support the growth of the city," he said.

"We are really passionate about Norwich as a creative city and Norfolk as a creative county.

"We are joint citizens of this place. Our history is about serving the people of this place.

"It's about protecting access to certain jobs, skills and careers and it's about playing our part in being a powerful voice in the amazing region we have."

articles.title: En 2009, Hugh Jackman dejó de ser el único actor que ha interpretado a Lobezno: así es Troye Sivan, el 'Logan' que nadie recuerda

articles.summary: El actor sudafricano tiene 31 años y más de 15 millones de seguidores solo en Instagram
articles.body: Para millones de espectadores, el nombre de Lobezno está indisolublemente ligado a la imponente figura de Hugh Jackman. Durante más de dos décadas, el actor australiano ha encarnado al mutante de las garras de adamantio, convirtiéndose en el rostro indiscutible de la franquicia. Sin embargo, la historia cinematográfica del personaje guarda un curioso secreto que pocos recuerdan: no ha sido el único en darle vida en la gran pantalla. En 2009, la película 'X-Men Orígenes: Lobezno' buscaba explorar el turbulento pasado del héroe desde sus primeros años de infancia. Para interpretar al joven James Howlett antes de manifestar plenamente sus habilidades y adoptar su famoso alias, la producción fichó a un jovencísimo talento sudafricano de apenas catorce años llamado Troye Sivan. Su aparición en el prólogo del filme capturó el dramático momento en que el personaje descubre sus poderes mutantes tras un trágico suceso familiar. En aquel momento, el nombre de Troye Sivan no decía mucho al público general fuera de Australia, el país en el que vivió desde los dos años cuando sus padres se mudaron a la ciudad de Perth. El prometedor actor emergente apenas daba sus primeros pasos en la industria del entretenimiento tras haberse dado a conocer en concursos de talento locales y en las primeras etapas de YouTube. Nadie imaginaba entonces que aquel niño de mirada desgarradora que interpretaba al futuro Lobezno acabaría tomando un camino profesional muy distinto al del cine de superhéroes. Con el paso de los años, Sivan dejó a un lado las garras de ficción para convertirse en una de las mayores superestrellas de la música pop internacional. Temas de éxito global, nominaciones a los premios Grammy y millones de seguidores en todo el mundo consolidaron al artista no solo como un referente musical, sino también como un icono global de la cultura y la visibilidad LGTBQ+. Su faceta interpretativa continuó de forma puntual, pero su identidad como estrella del pop terminó por eclipsar su debut en Marvel. Hoy en día, revisar el prólogo de la primera película en solitario de Lobezno supone un ejercicio de nostalgia y sorpresa para los fans de la cultura pop. Descubrir al icónico héroe del cómic encarnado por uno de los cantantes más influyentes de la actualidad es un detalle fascinante que permanece oculto a la vista de todos: un curioso cruce de caminos donde las garras de Lobezno abrieron paso a una estrella del pop mundial.

articles.title: ‘Hanuman Ansh’ Box Office Day 47: Neem Karoli Baba film beats ‘Toxic’ to cross Rs 366 crore globally
articles.summary: ‘Hanuman Ansh’, the devotional film directed by Vishal Chaturvedi and starring Shobhinaw Satyaa as spiritual guru Neem Karoli Baba, is on an unstoppab.
articles.body: ‘Hanuman Ansh’, the devotional film directed by Vishal Chaturvedi and starring Shobhinaw Satyaa as spiritual guru Neem Karoli Baba, is on an unstoppable record-breaking streak at the box office, both in India and abroad. Now in its 47th day of theatrical release, the film has earned Rs 331.70 crore gross and Rs 280.93 crore net domestically, pushing its global total to Rs 366.45 crore.'Hanuman Ansh' box office day 47 collectionThe film remains steady even in its seventh week, collecting Rs 4.90 crore from 7,702 screens on day 47 (seventh Tuesday), marking an 18% jump from the Rs 4.15 crore it earned on day 46 (seventh Monday). This, however, followed a sharp drop of nearly 70% from its day 45 (seventh Sunday) collection of Rs 13.75 crore, which itself was a notable rise over the Rs 9.75 crore earned on day 44 (seventh Saturday), up further from the Rs 5 crore collected on day 43 (seventh Friday).Day wise collections for 'Hanuman Ansh'Week 1: Rs. 1.08 croreWeek 2: Rs. 0.40 croreWeek 3: Rs. 10.40 croreWeek 4: Rs. 61.00 croreWeek 5: Rs. 90.25 croreWeek 6: Rs. 80.25 croreDay 43: Rs. 5.00 croreDay 44: Rs. 9.75 croreDay 45: Rs. 13.75 croreDay 46: Rs. 4.15 croreDay 47: Rs. 0.30 croreTOTAL: Rs. 276.33 crore'Hanuman Ansh' week 7 box office trendBased on the current trend, Week 7 earnings are expected to fall well short of Week 6's Rs 80.25 crore, which had already dipped from Week 5's Rs 90.25 crore, the film's best weekly haul so far. That figure marked a 30% jump from Week 4's Rs 61 crore, which in turn was over six times higher than the Rs 10.40 crore collected in Week 3.'Hanuman Ansh' vs 'Toxic' box office clash‘Hanuman Ansh’ has played a significant part in slowing down what could have been last month's box office juggernaut, Geethu Mohandas' pan-India action thriller ‘Toxic: A Fairytale for Grownups’. Featuring an ensemble cast including Yash, Nayanthara, Kiara Advani, Huma Qureshi, Rukmini Vasanth, and Tara Sutaria, the film hit theatres across several major Indian languages on August 26.'Hanuman Ansh' emerges as a sleeper hitBy that point, though already in its third week, ‘Hanuman Ansh’ saw a surge in daily collections on its third Sunday, crossing the Rs 1 crore mark for the first time with Rs 2.5 crore. From there, the sleeper hit didn't look back, going on to earn Rs 10.40 crore in Week 3, a sharp jump from its opening week collection of Rs 1.08 crore and Week 2's Rs 40 lakh, according to Sacnilk.'Hanuman Ansh' surpasses 'Toxic' worldwideCurrently in its seventh week of release, ‘Hanuman Ansh’ has steadily edged past Toxic's box office numbers, both in India and globally. The film's worldwide total now stands at Rs 366.45 crore, exceeding the Yash-starrer's Rs 342.07 crore by more than Rs 24 crore. Apart from ‘Toxic’, ‘Hanuman Ansh’ has also surpassed other big-ticket releases such as Sunny Deol's ‘Batwara 1947’, Emraan Hashmi's ‘Awarapan 2’, Saif Ali Khan and Akshay Kumar's ‘Haiwaan’, and Kunal Kemmu's ‘Vibe’.'Hanuman Ansh' international release and earnings‘Hanuman Ansh’ was released only in India to begin with, until Hombale Films took on its international distribution following the film's unexpected domestic boom in Week 3.
